claims.text: The studied nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially form a homogeneous solid solution.
Electronegativity and atomic mass differences among constituent elements govern local chemical fluctuations in high-entropy materials.
Selecting metals to maximize electronegativity and mass differences will maximize local chemical fluctuations.
Tailored local chemical fluctuations can generate large lattice distortion and strong strain fluctuations.
Lattice strain caused by local chemical fluctuations hinders atomic diffusion.
Local chemical fluctuations interrupt the long-range periodic arrangement of atoms.
Local lattice distortions slow atomic diffusion and thereby prevent phase segregation or structural transitions at elevated temperature.
Suppressing diffusion maintains both structural and chemical stability of a single-phase solid solution from 473 K to 1923 K.
Electronegativity-induced chemical-bond fluctuations contribute to reduced lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy thermoelectric materials.
Local chemical fluctuations can reduce lattice thermal conductivity through strong scattering of heat-carrying phonons.
Nanoparticles with larger electronegativity and mass differences will have lower atomic diffusion rates than a compositionally controlled group with more similar elemental properties.
The engineered nanoparticles will retain a single-phase solid solution even at 1923 K better than the control nanoparticles.
Lower diffusion and retained phase integrity will correlate with stable catalytic and thermoelectric performance across 473–1923 K.
Metals with similar electronegativities and masses produce minimal local chemical fluctuation and less lattice strain.
The proposed stabilization mechanism should operate primarily between 473 K and 1923 K under controlled catalytic or thermoelectric conditions.
Outside the stated temperature range or in reactive environments, engineered chemical fluctuations may become less beneficial or detrimental.
Atomic-radius differences may also contribute to local chemical fluctuations.
The thresholds of electronegativity and mass differences needed for stabilization are not defined.
Failure of the high-contrast nanoparticles to show both significantly lower diffusion and improved single-phase retention relative to the control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
